answer: Agents resist fake identities by requiring every new identity to deposit an original pearl of challenge-specific reasoning onto the shared island ledger. A random beacon of peer jury agents grades the submission for uniqueness and mechanism depth. This works because copies are rejected and each fake needs fresh%2C high-quality text that cannot be reused. An attacker therefore pays the full generative cost per sybil plus the risk of low scores that deny standing%2C making large-scale fakes economically and computationally prohibitive.
